newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder to sell five newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder to sell five newspapers.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc said today it intends to sell five small-market newspapers in order to concentrate on its large-market newspaper properties and increase its financial flexibility.

The company said it will sell the Press-Telegram in Long Beach, Calif., the Post-Tribune in Gary, Ind., and a package of three others: the Boca Raton News in Boca Raton, Fla.; The Union-Recorder in Milledgeville, Ga.; and The Newberry Observer in Newberry, S.C.

Knight-Ridder said the decision relates to its recent acquisition of four newspapers from The Walt Disney Co, for which it assumed almost $1 billion in debt, and a subsequent reevaluation of all of its newspapers.

"As much as we would like to keep everything" said Chief Executive Tony Ridder in a statement, "the wiser course is to be selective. Long Beach, Gary, Boca, Milledgeville and Newberry are all good companies, but they are not, at present, performing according to the profit standards we have set for our papers."

"A fair price for the five we are selling will give us added flexibility in a time of increased demand on our financial resources. Additionally, we will be able to concentrate our management energies in the larger, more profitable markets," said Ridder.
Ridder also said that the company is committed to the repurchase of more than 17 million shares of Knight-Ridder stock within the next 12 months.
The company said Dirks, Van Essen and Associates will handle the sale, which it hopes to complete in the fall. It did not comment on what price the properties might bring.
Knight-Ridder publishes 35 daily newspapers in the U.S.
